summary: Backend-only end-to-end verification of the PKCE bug-fix. All 11 pytest tests pass (100%). Verified: (1) admin login + GET /api/drive/status returns {connected:true, configured:true}; (2) GET /api/drive/connect returns a Google authorization_url with scope drive.file, access_type=offline, and NO code_challenge param (PKCE disabled as intended); (3) patient (mario.rossi) upload to POST /api/dossiers/doss_fbbdfe2a258f/files returns a file entry with a non-null drive_file_id, proving the stored OAuth tokens actually work for Drive API writes (incl. any refresh); (4) GET /api/dossiers/doss_fbbdfe2a258f/files/{file_id} with patient cookie returns 200 + bytes; (5) GET /api/drive/callback with invalid code and with no params still redirects (307) to /admin?drive=error — graceful error handling intact.
critical_code_review_comments: PKCE fix looks correct: _drive_flow(autogenerate_code_verifier=False) is used in both /connect and /callback so no code_verifier is required across the two Flow instances — verified by absence of code_challenge in the auth URL.

context_for_next_testing_agent: PKCE bug-fix is fully verified end-to-end. Drive OAuth tokens are persisted and working. If Drive is disconnected in the future, TestDriveUploadSuccess will fail with drive_file_id=null — that would indicate token refresh or re-consent is required.
rca of the issue: Original callback error 'invalid_grant: Missing code verifier' happened because google-auth-oauthlib's Flow auto-generated a PKCE code_verifier at /drive/connect time but a brand-new Flow instance in /drive/callback had no memory of it. Fix (verified): both endpoints now instantiate Flow with autogenerate_code_verifier=False, so no code_challenge is sent at auth time and no code_verifier is expected at token-exchange time. End-to-end proof: successful upload returned drive_file_id, meaning the tokens stored from the PKCE-less callback are valid for real Drive API calls.
